clue.text: Get rid of game of skill — here's game of chance

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
Go is the Japanese board game of strategy

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a game of skill and turns to gambling instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbers-calling hall game is won purely by luck, a textbook example of a game of chance.

clue.text: Victorian scientist in multiple books about a period in history

indicators.note: about says the books go round the letter a

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so several make BBB
an age is an era or period of history

explanation.surface: A Victorian scientist appears in many history books about one era.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Babbage designed the Difference and Analytical Engines, early mechanical computers of the Victorian age.

clue.text: Semi-desert, say, occupying half of Nevada

indicators.note: occupying puts the example word inside the half state name
half of takes the first three letters of the state name

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A dry region, for instance, covering half of Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: The arid southern region of Israel is a semi-desert.

clue.text: Ace at sea entering current appropriate for sea

indicators.note: entering puts the scrambled letters inside the current word

parts.note: ongoing means current or in progress

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of ace are mixed

explanation.surface: A star sailor joins a current fit for the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like the star sailor, but 'at sea' scrambles it to CEA, which goes in after the O of the current word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships designed to cross the open ocean rather than coastal waters are suited to the sea.

clue.text: Consequential worry about Eastern leader lacking force

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is dropped from what has been built so far
about says the worry word goes round the leader

parts.note: to fret is to worry
a sultan is a ruler in the Muslim East
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A writer frets over the consequences of some Eastern ruler losing his army.
explanation.walkthrough: FRET placed 'about' SULTAN gives FRESULTANT; 'lacking force' then takes away the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resultant follows as an outcome, the same idea as consequential.

clue.text: Communist question not initially observed in powerful piece

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: seen means observed

explanation.surface: A communist's question about a powerful chessman went unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is the strongest chess piece, and in Lewis Carroll's Looking-Glass the red one is a commanding figure.

clue.text: Limits to security dishearten every Australian city

indicators.note: limits to takes the first and last letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Restrictions on safety dismay a whole Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in Australia, capital of New South Wales.

clue.text: European in China upset over pressure

indicators.note: over in a down clue sets the first piece above the second
upset in a down clue turns the friend word upwards

parts.note: in cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, so pal
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A European in China is upset by stress.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for the Sámi people of northern Scandinavia, so a European.

clue.text: Maiden threatened, note, circled by a camel leaving tracks

indicators.note: circled by says the note goes inside the camel phrase
leaving means the railway letters depart from the camel word

parts.note: a dromedary is a one-humped camel
RY abbreviates railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: A camel walks away from a threatened maiden, leaving its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this princess was chained to a rock as prey for a sea monster until Perseus saved her.

clue.text: Tense reprimand has you blubbing

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an earful is a scolding

explanation.surface: A tense telling-off leaves you in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubbing is crying noisily, so someone blubbing is in tears.

clue.text: Egocentric British, stupid to give up power

indicators.note: to give up here means one letter yields its place to another

parts.note: pigheaded means obstinately stupid
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A jibe that the British are self-centred and dim enough to surrender power.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of PIGHEADED gives way to B.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person is said to have a swollen head, so being self-important and egocentric go together.

clue.text: Italian city apartment, one behind university

indicators.note: behind places the word for one after the university letter

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or apartment
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note on an Italian flat for one person, located behind the university.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in the Veneto region is famous for its ancient university and its basilica of St Anthony.

clue.text: Religious commemoration sure to rearrange exciting events

parts.note: Advent is the church season before Christmas

indicators.note: to rearrange tells us the letters of sure are put in another order

explanation.surface: A church festival that is bound to shake up the calendar of exciting events.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapades and exploits full of risk and excitement are synonyms for these exciting events.

clue.text: Idle fool on line

indicators.note: in an across clue, the fool placed on the line follows it

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy, stupid person

explanation.surface: A lazy fool hanging about on the phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to lounge about doing nothing, a common verb synonym.

clue.text: Fail to appreciate university revue and upset about lecturer

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the lecturer letter
upset means the letters of revue and are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A college comedy show offends the staff, who fail to appreciate it.
explanation.definitionFit: To underrate something is to fail to see its true worth.

clue.text: How'd you like your eggs? (No problems ahead of deliveries)

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first word before the second

parts.note: easy means without difficulty
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: A waiter asks about breakfast eggs, while the bracket reads like a courier's promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an answer to the question: fried eggs flipped briefly so the yolk stays runny.
explanation.definitionFit: An American diner style of fried egg, turned once and cooked lightly, is one reply to how you want them.

clue.text: Insightful story I used in company (American)

parts.note: a saga is a long story

indicators.note: used in places the letter inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: A tale told in an American firm offers insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, wise and perceptive is a dictionary sense of insightful.

clue.text: Strange — not what you'd expect from a King — not good

indicators.note: the second not says a letter is left out

parts.words: what you'd expect from a King
parts.note: regal means kingly, so unregal is unkingly

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a monarch's behaviour was odd and poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreal is used informally for something so bizarre it is hard to believe, hence strange.

clue.text: Right to tuck into ice-cream and wine, with no real options available?

indicators.note: to tuck into means the letter goes inside the ice-cream word

parts.note: a cone is an ice-cream cornet
red is red wine

explanation.surface: Someone at a dessert stall with only ice cream and wine to choose from.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapped with no way out, as in being backed into a corner.

clue.text: English item of ordnance, excluding first machine

indicators.note: excluding first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a mine is an explosive weapon, an item of military ordnance

explanation.surface: An English piece of artillery is set aside in favour of a first machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor or device that converts energy into motion is a machine.

clue.text: Enthusiastic: sent message expressing first time touring Channel Islands

indicators.note: touring means the shortened message word goes around the islands
expressing means squeezing out, here the opening letter

parts.note: texted means sent a message by phone
T is the physics symbol for time
CI abbreviates the Channel Islands, British islands off Normandy

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly texts about their first trip around Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressing' is used in its squeezing-out sense: the first time letter is pressed out, leaving EXTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and thrilled is a close synonym of enthusiastic.

clue.text: British radio astronomer missing last line by excellent poet

indicators.note: missing last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Sir Bernard Lovell founded the Jodrell Bank radio telescope
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An astronomer skips the final line of a fine poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link meaning next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was a 17th-century Cavalier poet, author of To Althea, from Prison.

clue.text: Electroplated strange green table decoration

parts.note: EP is the hallmark abbreviation for electroplated

indicators.note: strange means the letters of green appear oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A silver-plated dish in an odd shade of green decorates the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental centrepiece with branching dishes for fruit or sweets is a table decoration.

clue.text: Theatrical lawyer left one arraigned at the outset

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: at the outset picks the first letter of arraigned

explanation.surface: A stage barrister abandons a defendant at the start of the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice the heroine disguises herself as a lawyer to defend Antonio, a stage advocate.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot male

definitions.meaning: to raise the hammer ready for firing

explanation.surface: Getting a gun ready for a male bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer is raised before firing a gun, and the same word names a male fowl.

clue.text: Collusion to study transport in French city

parts.note: to con is to study carefully, especially a text

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the city name

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
a van is a vehicle, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A plot to research traffic in a French city looks like secret scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretly allowing or cooperating in wrongdoing is collusion.

clue.text: Loves to embrace a symbol of hardness

indicators.note: to embrace means hold inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so nils

explanation.surface: Lovers hugging seems the opposite of toughness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom hard as nails makes these metal spikes a byword for toughness.

clue.text: Bowled by high ball, nothing scored?

parts.note: B is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for bowled
a lob is a ball hit or thrown high

explanation.surface: A batsman is bowled by a lofted ball without scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket slang a zero score, a duck, is also called this, from the shape of the 0.

clue.text: Unwanted commentator initially ready to probe numbers killed

indicators.note: to probe means to go into, so one letter goes inside the casualty word

parts.note: the death toll is the number of people killed

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of ready

explanation.surface: An unwelcome reporter is ready to dig into casualty figures.
explanation.definitionFit: An online provocateur posts unwanted comments to stir up trouble.

clue.text: Sensational fact about stream

indicators.note: about says the fact word goes round the stream word

parts.note: a thing can mean a fact or matter
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An amazing truth concerning a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exciting and gripping is sensational.

clue.text: Panel get on after a blow

indicators.note: after places the boarding word behind the blow

parts.note: a dash can be a sudden violent blow or stroke
to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to climb aboard after being struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument panel facing a car's driver is its fascia or dashboard.

clue.text: To follow European purpose round will engage Nationalist

indicators.note: will engage means the result takes the letter inside it
round tells us the two pieces together are turned backwards

parts.note: use means purpose, as in what is the use

explanation.surface: A European cause is turning to take on a Nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: E + USE turned 'round' gives ESUE; N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result is to follow.
